result.question: How do I prepare ORS solution?
result.questionEn: How do I prepare ORS solution?

steps.text: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Pour the entire contents of a packet of ORS into a clean container (a mixing bowl or jar) for mixing the ORS.
Measure 1 litre of clean water (or correct amount for packet used).
Pour the water into the container.

result.question: How much ORS solution should the child drink after each loose stool?
result.questionEn: How much ORS solution should the child drink after each loose stool?

steps.text: Advise the caregiver to give as much ORS solution as the child wants. But give at least 1/2 cup of a 250 ml cup (about 125 ml) after each loose stool.
She should try to give at least ½ cup after each loose stool.
Give 2 extra packets of ORS to the caregiver to take home, in case she needs to prepare more.

result.question: What should the caregiver do if the child vomits while taking ORS?
result.questionEn: What should the caregiver do if the child vomits while taking ORS?

steps.text: If the child vomits, advise the caregiver to wait 10 minutes before giving more ORS solution.
steps.textSw: Mtoto akitapika, mshauri mlezi asubiri dakika 10 kabla ya kumpa myeyusho zaidi wa ORS.

steps.text: Then start giving the solution again, but more slowly.
steps.textSw: Kisha aanze kumpa myeyusho tena, lakini polepole zaidi.

steps.text: She should offer the child as much as the child will take, or at least ½ cup ORS solution after each loose stool.
steps.textSw: Ampe mtoto kiasi chochote atakachokunywa, au angalau nusu kikombe cha myeyusho wa ORS baada ya kila haja kubwa ya maji.

result.question: A child with fever has a negative RDT and no danger sign. What should I do?
result.questionEn: A child with fever has a negative RDT and no danger sign. What should I do?

steps.text: If the child has had fever for less than 7 days and the results of the RDT are negative, or the child lives in a non-malaria area, then ask to see the child in 3 days for a follow-up visit.
Also advise the caregiver to bring the child back right away if the child becomes sicker.
During the follow-up visit, look for signs of illness again.
If the child is not better when you see the child during the follow-up visit, refer the child to a health facility.

result.question: When should I follow up a child I treated at home?
result.questionEn: When should I follow up a child I treated at home?

steps.text: Ask the caregiver to bring the child back to see you in 3 days for a follow-up visit, even if the child improves.
If the family cannot come, perhaps a neighbour might be willing to bring the child to see you.
If not, you must go to visit the child at home, especially if you have given the child an antimalarial or antibiotic.
If the child continues treatment at home, write the next follow-up day.
